Interesting — the reference sheet directly gives I = ζ(3). But I need to verify this and compute J. Let me work through both integrals systematically.

## Integral I

We have I = ∫₀¹ ln(x)·ln(1-x)/x dx.

Using the series expansion: ln(1-x) = -∑_{n≥1} xⁿ/n, for |x| < 1.

So:
I = ∫₀¹ ln(x)/x · (-∑_{n≥1} xⁿ/n) dx = -∑_{n≥1} (1/n) ∫₀¹ ln(x) x^{n-1} dx

Now, ∫₀¹ ln(x) x^{n-1} dx. Let's compute this. Using integration by parts or the known result: ∫₀¹ x^{a-1} ln(x) dx = -1/a².

Indeed: ∫₀¹ x^{a-1} dx = 1/a. Differentiate w.r.t. a: ∫₀¹ x^{a-1} ln(x) dx = -1/a².

So with a = n: ∫₀¹ ln(x) x^{n-1} dx = -1/n².

Thus:
I = -∑_{n≥1} (1/n) · (-1/n²) = ∑_{n≥1} 1/n³ = ζ(3).

So I = ζ(3) ≈ 1.2020569.

## Integral J

J = ∫₀¹ ln(x)² · ln(1-x)/x dx.

Again use ln(1-x) = -∑_{n≥1} xⁿ/n:

J = ∫₀¹ ln(x)²/x · (-∑_{n≥1} xⁿ/n) dx = -∑_{n≥1} (1/n) ∫₀¹ ln(x)² x^{n-1} dx.

Now we need ∫₀¹ ln(x)² x^{n-1} dx. Starting from ∫₀¹ x^{a-1} dx = 1/a, differentiate twice w.r.t. a:

First derivative: ∫₀¹ x^{a-1} ln(x) dx = -1/a².

Second derivative: ∫₀¹ x^{a-1} ln(x)² dx = 2/a³.

So with a = n: ∫₀¹ ln(x)² x^{n-1} dx = 2/n³.

Thus:
J = -∑_{n≥1} (1/n) · (2/n³) = -2 ∑_{n≥1} 1/n⁴ = -2 ζ(4).

And ζ(4) = π⁴/90, so:
J = -2π⁴/90 = -π⁴/45.

Numerically: π⁴ ≈ 97.409091, so -π⁴/45 ≈ -2.164646...
